bull.b: Repeatable piloted transition flights under U.K. CAA oversight and a second full-scale prototype materially advance technical validation. Higher test capacity can accelerate evidence gathering, support certification work, and reduce execution risk as Vertical progresses toward commercial aircraft development.

Progress toward pilot assembly and a larger battery facility shows the company is building capabilities beyond prototype design. Expanded internal battery capacity, government support discussions, and ecosystem programs could improve manufacturing readiness and support a scalable platform across electric and hybrid variants.

Fresh financing and available cash provide resources to fund certification, testing, manufacturing readiness, and hybrid development over the next several quarters. Although the capital does not establish self-funded operations, it improves near-term continuity for executing the defined Valo milestone roadmap.

bear.b: A one-year certification delay postpones the point at which Vertical can deliver aircraft and begin recognizing meaningful commercial revenue. It also extends development spending, increases the time exposed to execution risk, and makes the company dependent on additional capital before commercialization can begin.

The projected burn rate indicates that operations remain far from self-funding while aircraft testing, certification, battery work, and manufacturing investments continue. Sustained negative cash generation reduces financial flexibility and means progress toward the 2029 target will require further funding or tighter spending.

Minimal revenue and ongoing operating deficits show that the business has not yet achieved commercial scale or proven recurring earnings power. Negative equity and deeply negative free cash flow compound the weakness, leaving future value dependent on certification, production ramp-up, and customer conversion.
